summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, neurogenic bladder with chronic indwelling Foley catheter, paraplegia, and polysubstance abuse was admitted for recurrent left flank pain and an intensely itchy rash. She had been discharged recently after treatment for pyelonephritis with cefpodoxime but returned with persistent symptoms. Evaluation revealed pyelonephritis due to multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterococcus, confirmed by urine culture. A renal ultrasound showed no abscess or obstruction. She was started on IV meropenem and linezolid for a planned 14-day course. The rash was diagnosed as scabies and treated with permethrin cream, with improvement. Lactic acidosis on admission resolved with IV fluids. Due to her history of narcotic-seeking behavior, pain was managed with acetaminophen and limited oral dilaudid. After extensive counseling on the risks of incomplete antibiotic treatment, including sepsis and death, she chose to leave against medical advice on hospital day 7, having completed only 6 of 14 antibiotic days. She was discharged to extended care with instructions to continue insulin, resume metformin, manage constipation, and monitor for infection recurrence.
